name: Priya Osei-Lindqvist
description: Priya Osei-Lindqvist spent seven years producing 'Same City,' a long-form neural-feed documentary series in which she spent three consecutive months living at each tier of M88, from a Shelf squat in the Caldwell districts to a borrowed Spire residence obtained through a contact she refuses to name. Her documentation style is intimate and slow — no narration, no editorial commentary, just lived days rendered in full BCI-immersive format so that viewers experience each tier's texture, smell, and social rhythm from inside. She was born Tier 3 and makes no attempt to hide that origin or the privilege it represents.
cultural_impact: The 'Same City' series is widely credited with shifting M88 public opinion on Shelf living conditions more effectively than any political campaign, because it makes the Shelf's reality experientially accessible to Tier 3 and 4 viewers rather than abstractly legible. Corporate media has responded by funding competing 'both sides' documentary series, which have been almost universally panned.
key_figures: Tomás Achebe-Reinholt (her sound and environmental capture technician)
Yael Okonkwo-Bergström (her Tier 5 contact, identity protected)
locations: Vantec-Meridian Media Tower (site of her only corporate interview, which she walked out of)
story_hooks: Priya's unaired footage from her Spire months contains something she wasn't meant to see — and her Tier 5 contact is now pressuring her to destroy it, or lose the access that made the series possible.
A Shelf resident who appears extensively in 'Same City' has gone missing, and Priya has reason to believe their visibility in her documentary made them a target.

A corponation offers to fund a second season of 'Same City' with full creative control guaranteed in writing — and Priya has to decide whether that guarantee is worth the paper of the contract it's written on.
platform: Same City (BCI-immersive neural-feed documentary series, independent distribution)
controversy: During her Tier 4 residency segment, Priya documented a building manager systematically falsifying safety inspections in a way that directly implicated a mid-tier corponation subsidiary. She published the footage without legal review. The resulting lawsuit was settled out of court, the terms sealed, and Priya has never publicly confirmed what she received or conceded — though the building manager was quietly transferred.
